source_columns: birthplace, birthplacet, mabirth, mabirtht.q, pabirth, pabirtht.q, sn, wave
expression:
local({
  child_code <- as.numeric(birthplace)
  mother_code <- as.numeric(mabirth)
  father_code <- as.numeric(pabirth)
  child <- case_when(
    child_code == 1 ~ "in",
    child_code %in% 2:6 ~ "abroad",
    child_code == 7 & grepl("singapore|bugis", tolower(birthplacet)) ~ NA_character_,
    child_code == 7 ~ "abroad"
  )
  mother <- case_when(
    mother_code == 1 ~ "in",
    mother_code %in% 2:6 ~ "abroad",
    mother_code == 7 & grepl("singapore|bugis", tolower(mabirtht.q)) ~ NA_character_,
    mother_code == 7 ~ "abroad"
  )
  father <- case_when(
    father_code == 1 ~ "in",
    father_code %in% 2:6 ~ "abroad",
    father_code == 7 & grepl("singapore|bugis", tolower(pabirtht.q)) ~ NA_character_,
    father_code == 7 ~ "abroad"
  )
  background <- case_when(
    mother %in% "in" | father %in% "in" ~ "Native",
    is.na(mother) & is.na(father) ~ NA_character_,
    child %in% "in" ~ "Second-generation",
    child %in% "abroad" ~ "First-generation"
  )
  coalesce(carry_within(background, sn, order = as.numeric(wave)), "Unknown")
})
notes: Wave 2 items, carried within child to waves 1 and 3 (carry-forward rule): child's (birthplace), biological mother's (mabirth) and biological father's (pabirth) place of birth, Singapore, Malaysia, India, China, USA, Europe, others (specify), don't know. Singapore = in the country; other places abroad; 'others' text naming Singapore or Bugis ('Singapore PR', 'Bangkok / Singapore', 'Bugis') and don't know = unknown. One parent unknown: the other decides. Children not seen at wave 2 = Unknown.

Child's place of birth (birthplace), wave 2 only, carried within child to waves 1 and 3 (carry-forward rule): Singapore = Yes; Malaysia, India, China, USA, Europe and other countries = No; 'others' text 'Singapore PR' and don't know = Unknown; children not seen at wave 2 = Unknown.

source_columns: timem, timea, timee, timewknm, timewkna, timewkne, oftenplay
expression:
local({
  blank <- is.na(timem) & is.na(timea) & is.na(timee) & is.na(timewknm) & is.na(timewkna) & is.na(timewkne)
  never <- blank & as.numeric(oftenplay) %in% c(8, 9)
  hours <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5.5, 6)
  wd <- cbind(as.numeric(timem), as.numeric(timea), as.numeric(timee))
  we <- cbind(as.numeric(timewknm), as.numeric(timewkna), as.numeric(timewkne))
  wd[wd == 6.5] <- 6
  we[we == 6.5] <- 6
  wd[!wd %in% hours] <- NA
  we[!we %in% hours] <- NA
  if_else(never, 0, rowSums(wd))
})
notes: Child self-report, every wave: 'On a usual school day, how many hours do you play computer/video games in the morning?' and the afternoon and evening items (Gentile et al. 2011, Appendix: response 'Hours'). Sum of timem, timea, timee (DR-0002). Codes are hours: 0 'none' = 0; codes 0.5-4 carry no label in the file and their wording is not documented, so they are read as hour bands at the value coded; 4.5 '4 to 5 hours' and 5.5 '5 to 6 hours' at their band midpoints; top band 'more than 6 hours' (coded 6.5) = 6 per daypart; an undefined code (5.6, three wave-3 weekend answers) = NA. 'computer/video games' gives no device list, so the items cover gaming on any device. Wave 1 releases no missing values on these items (waves 2-3: 9-11% missing); 22% of wave-1 children are 0 on all six against 8-10% later, so some wave-1 zeros may be unanswered. Waves 2-3: children answering never or no longer playing with the time items blank take 0 (non-users rule; 182 child-waves). The frequency item 'how often do you play video games' (oftenplay, waves 2-3) disagrees with the time items even for never-players, so the items are read as usual-day time and are not scaled by days played; oftenplay is otherwise unused. The study's capped sums (VG_weekday, VG_weekend, VG_WK) and the per-favourite-game times (timemf1-timemf3, timess1-timess3, eachtm1-eachtm3) are not used here; the per-game times feed the st_violent_game rows.

source_columns: timemf1, timemf2, timemf3, gm1genre, gm2genre, gm3genre, oftenplay, wave
expression:
local({
  shooter <- c(3, 4, 11, 13)
  hours <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5.5, 6.5, 7.5, 8.5, 9.5, 10)
  answered <- !is.na(timemf1) | !is.na(timemf2) | !is.na(timemf3)
  never <- !answered & as.numeric(oftenplay) %in% c(8, 9)
  time <- cbind(as.numeric(timemf1), as.numeric(timemf2), as.numeric(timemf3))
  time[time == 10.5] <- 10
  time[!time %in% hours] <- NA
  genre <- cbind(as.numeric(gm1genre), as.numeric(gm2genre), as.numeric(gm3genre))
  part <- ifelse(matrix(genre %in% shooter, ncol = 3), time, 0)
  case_when(wave == "3" ~ NA_real_, never ~ 0, !answered ~ NA_real_, .default = rowSums(part))
})
notes: Waves 1-2, child self-report: 'on a usual school day, how many hours do you play this game' for each of the three favourite games the child named (timemf1-timemf3), summed over the games the study's genre coding (gm1genre-gm3genre) places among shooters: first-person shooter, third-person shooter and the hybrids FPSTPG and FPSRPG (codes 3, 4, 11, 13); other and uncoded games count as non-violent (sum over titles, DR-0002). Codes are hours: 0 'none' = 0; codes 0.5-4 carry no label in the file and are read as hour bands at the value coded, as on the gaming-time items; labelled bands '4 to 5 hours' to '9 to 10 hours' (4.5-9.5) at their midpoints; top band 'more than 10 hours' (coded 10.5) = 10 per game. Partial: named favourite games only, classified by a violent genre (shooters). Wave 3 releases no game names or genre codes: NA. Wave 2: children answering never or no longer playing (oftenplay) with no per-game time take 0 (non-users rule). The per-game kill-frequency ratings and ESRB ratings do not classify games here; they feed st_violent_game_index.

  hours <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5.5, 6.5, 7.5, 8.5, 9.5, 10)
  violent <- matrix(cbind(as.numeric(gm1genre), as.numeric(gm2genre), as.numeric(gm3genre)) %in% shooter, ncol = 3)
  wd <- cbind(as.numeric(timemf1), as.numeric(timemf2), as.numeric(timemf3))
  we <- cbind(as.numeric(timess1), as.numeric(timess2), as.numeric(timess3))
  wd[wd == 10.5] <- 10
  we[we == 10.5] <- 10
  wd[!wd %in% hours] <- NA
  we[!we %in% hours] <- NA
  wd_answered <- !is.na(timemf1) | !is.na(timemf2) | !is.na(timemf3)
  we_answered <- !is.na(timess1) | !is.na(timess2) | !is.na(timess3)
  never <- as.numeric(oftenplay) %in% c(8, 9)
  wd_hours <- case_when(
    wave == "3" ~ NA_real_,
    never & !wd_answered ~ 0,
    !wd_answered ~ NA_real_,
    .default = rowSums(ifelse(violent, wd, 0))
  )
  we_hours <- case_when(
    wave == "3" ~ NA_real_,
    never & !we_answered ~ 0,
    !we_answered ~ NA_real_,
    .default = rowSums(ifelse(violent, we, 0))
  )
  (5 * wd_hours + 2 * we_hours) / 7
})

local({
  answered <- cbind(
    !is.na(timemf1) | !is.na(timess1) | !is.na(fc3) | !is.na(fc4),
    !is.na(timemf2) | !is.na(timess2) | !is.na(fd3) | !is.na(fd4),
    !is.na(timemf3) | !is.na(timess3) | !is.na(fe3) | !is.na(fe4)
  )
  timed <- cbind(
    !is.na(timemf1) | !is.na(timess1),
    !is.na(timemf2) | !is.na(timess2),
    !is.na(timemf3) | !is.na(timess3)
  )
  rated <- cbind(!is.na(fc3) | !is.na(fc4), !is.na(fd3) | !is.na(fd4), !is.na(fe3) | !is.na(fe4))
  none <- cbind(
    as.numeric(timemf1) %in% 0 & as.numeric(timess1) %in% 0,
    as.numeric(timemf2) %in% 0 & as.numeric(timess2) %in% 0,
    as.numeric(timemf3) %in% 0 & as.numeric(timess3) %in% 0
  )
  scored <- none | (timed & rated)
  never <- rowSums(answered) == 0 & as.numeric(oftenplay) %in% c(8, 9)
  case_when(never ~ 0, 2 * rowSums(scored) >= rowSums(answered) ~ as.numeric(VGEsr), .default = NA_real_)
})

local({
  n <- length(slpwk.q)
  s <- gsub(":", ".", gsub("\\s+", "", tolower(c(slpwk.q, wakewk.q))))
  ok <- grepl("^[0-9]{1,2}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?(-[0-9]{1,2}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?)?$", s)
  ends <- c(sub("-.*$", "", s), sub("^.*-", "", s))
  h <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("\\..*$", "", ends)))
  m <- ifelse(grepl(".", ends, fixed = TRUE), sub("^.*\\.", "", ends), "0")
  m <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ifelse(nchar(m) == 1, paste0(m, "0"), m)))
  value <- ifelse(h <= 24 & m < 60, h + m / 60, NA_real_)
  a <- value[seq_len(2 * n)]
  b <- value[2 * n + seq_len(2 * n)]
  b <- ifelse(b < a, b + 24, b)
  clock <- ifelse(ok, ((a + b) / 2) %% 24, NA_real_)
  parsed <- (clock[n + seq_len(n)] - clock[seq_len(n)]) %% 24
  if_else(wave == "2", parsed, as.numeric(nighthrs_wk))
})
notes: Child self-report, waves 2-3; wave 1 did not ask. 'What time do you sleep on a normal weekday' to 'what time do you wake up on a normal weekday' (slpwk.q, wakewk.q), wake minus sleep across midnight. Wave 3 times are released as seconds after midnight, and the study's duration (nighthrs_wk) equals wake minus sleep on every row, so it is used. Wave 2 clock text is read as a 24-hour clock, as the study's wave-3 coding reads it: 'h' or 'h.mm' (one digit after the point is tens of minutes, '22.3' = 22:30), a range ('22-23') at its midpoint; text such as '24 plus', '1 or 2' or 'varies' is NA (under 2% of answers). About ten bedtimes per item written on a 12-hour clock ('9', '10.30') are read as morning times, as at wave 3, and give durations over 16 hours, kept for screening at analysis.

expression:
local({
  n <- length(slpwk.q)
  s <- gsub(":", ".", gsub("\\s+", "", tolower(c(slpwk.q, wakewk.q, slpwkn.q, wakewkn.q))))
  ok <- grepl("^[0-9]{1,2}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?(-[0-9]{1,2}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?)?$", s)
  ends <- c(sub("-.*$", "", s), sub("^.*-", "", s))
  h <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("\\..*$", "", ends)))
  m <- ifelse(grepl(".", ends, fixed = TRUE), sub("^.*\\.", "", ends), "0")
  m <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ifelse(nchar(m) == 1, paste0(m, "0"), m)))
  value <- ifelse(h <= 24 & m < 60, h + m / 60, NA_real_)
  a <- value[seq_len(4 * n)]
  b <- value[4 * n + seq_len(4 * n)]
  b <- ifelse(b < a, b + 24, b)
  clock <- ifelse(ok, ((a + b) / 2) %% 24, NA_real_)
  school_night <- (clock[n + seq_len(n)] - clock[seq_len(n)]) %% 24
  weekend <- (clock[3 * n + seq_len(n)] - clock[2 * n + seq_len(n)]) %% 24
  if_else(
    wave == "2",
    (5 * school_night + 2 * weekend) / 7,
    (5 * as.numeric(nighthrs_wk) + 2 * as.numeric(nighthrs_wkn)) / 7
  )
})
